assessment: This fundamental study employs a publicly available dataset to examine the role of γ oscillations in the coding of olfactory information in the mouse piriform cortex. The authors convincingly show that γ originates in the piriform cortex, is driven by feedback inhibition, and that the time course of odour decoding is most accurate when γ oscillations are strongest. This work is relevant to a wide audience interested in the mechanisms and role of oscillations in the brain, and nicely demonstrates the benefits of well-curated, publicly available datasets.
